| f-17c3 | question | NA | ANSWERING O-PRIME'S AMPLIFICATION (mtime granularity and clock skew on ac-0003) — the implementation is BETTER than the plan's own wording and the hazard class is false-negative, never false-positive. The plan promised a check on whether daemon.key is 'newer than the listening daemon's boot TIME', which would have compared a filesystem mtime against a process clock — two different sources, exposed to exactly the skew I was asked to hunt. The code does not do that. `published_mtime` is the mtime of the key file itself, read immediately after `persist` (auth.rs:96-103), and the 401 compares that against the CURRENT mtime of the same file on the same filesystem (auth.rs:179-183). Same clock, same inode, so cross-source skew is structurally impossible. Working through the remaining cases: a coarse-granularity filesystem (1s mtime, e.g. HFS+) where daemon B overwrites within the same second yields equal mtimes and the check reports FALSE — the hint degrades to the honest generic 'read the current key / restart' message rather than asserting something untrue. A backward system-clock jump between two publications does the same. Both are false NEGATIVES: the operator loses the better hint, never gets a wrong one. A false POSITIVE requires the key file's mtime to advance while its BYTES still fail to authenticate — e.g. a backup or editor touching daemon.key without changing content, which cannot produce a 401 at all since a matching key short-circuits at auth.rs:174. I could not construct a realistic false positive. One micro-observation, not a defect: the 401 path performs a `std::fs::metadata` syscall per unauthorized request, so a wrong-key client in a retry loop stats the file each time; it is on the error path only. | crates/daemon/src/auth.rs:96-103 (`published_mtime` capture), :174 (authorized short-circuit), :179-183 (comparison), :37-47 (`Auth::new`, the test-daemon constructor, which reads the same file's mtime and so is equal-not-newer) | [x] checked | — | — | — | [acceptance-criteria](../../plan.dd.md#acceptance-criteria) | PROVEN BY MY OWN MUTATION plus a live A/B. Reverted, CODE-CLEAN. Live A/B against my scratch daemon on :60843: (a) wrong key with mtime forcibly held at the published value via os.utime produced the generic 'read the current key from &lt;path&gt; ... if the file is missing or stale, restart' hint with no overwrite claim; (b) wrong key with a fresh mtime produced 'another flowspace3 daemon overwrote the shared key at &lt;path&gt;; restart the daemon that owns :60843', naming the correct live port; (c) restoring the original bytes and mtime returned `flowspace3 ping` to exit 0. |
| f-17c4 | question | NIT | TWO RESIDUAL HOLES IN THE FENCE, both outside the ACs as written, neither blocking, recorded so they are decisions rather than oversights. (1) `run_sandbox()` calls NEITHER `refuse_a_defaulted_store_under_test` NOR `refuse_undesignated_production_store`. It reads the ambient database URL purely to select a server and credentials (boot.rs:328-340) and then mints a disposable child via `FreshDatabase::create_from`. So `flowspace3 daemon --sandbox` from a foreign cwd on a default config still CREATEs and DROPs a database on the production postmaster at :5433. It never uses the production database as its store and never touches the shared key, so no AC is violated and this behaviour predates the PR — but 'a foreign cwd cannot touch prod' is not literally true for the sandbox path. (2) `is_loopback` accepts any loopback IP, and `bind_address_accepts_every_loopback_spelling` pins 127.0.0.2 as valid. Two daemons sharing ONE config directory but configured with different loopback hosts (127.0.0.1 and 127.0.0.2) would both bind successfully and both publish into the same daemon.key. That is outside ac-0001, which scopes to 'the same config dir and port', and per-instance keys keyed by port are an explicit plan non-goal — the correct place to close it, if it is ever worth closing. | crates/daemon/src/boot.rs:217-267 (`run_sandbox`, no guard calls), :328-340 (ambient URL reuse), :863-868 (`is_loopback`), :944-955 (the 127.0.0.2 test) | [x] checked | — | — | — | [non-goals](../../plan.dd.md#non-goals) | Read at this sha; not executed — deliberately, since exercising `--sandbox` on the ambient config would have contacted the production postmaster, which this review's fence forbids.
